messages:
jordan_support: Heads-up — Acme Mobile opened a Sev2. They see intermittent p99 spikes only on streaming responses (SSE over h2). Non-streaming /v1/generate is fine. They provided a short repro and a capture showing a long pause after the first chunk. Repro: `curl --http2 -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":400}' -v`. sample: first byte at ~80ms, then next chunk at ~3.2s, then steady thereafter. Logs attached in ticket (snip below).

sarah_support: Thanks Jordan. Customer says this started yesterday after a platform deploy around 02:30 UTC. They can reproduce reliably with a small prompt. No auth/billing issues. P95 maybe fine, but p99 jumps ~2.5s for streaming only. :thinking:

mike_engineer: @sarah_support can you paste the raw proxy timestamped entries? wondering if this is proxy coalescing or TCP write buffering at the edge.

jordan_support: pasted minimal log snippet from their capture:
```
[2026-03-16T02:31:12.145Z] REQ id=abcd123 path=/v1/stream/generate client=acme mobile
[02:31:12.225Z] FIRST_CHUNK sent len=256
[02:31:15.420Z] CHUNK sent len=32
[02:31:15.430Z] CHUNK sent len=128
```
(so ~3.2s gap between first and second chunk)

ingrid_sre: That gap screams "coalescing" or Nagle-ish behavior. Which edge/proxy did the request hit? Any envs using the new coalescing tuning rolled out yesterday?

sarah_support: Customer zone is us-west-2, routed through our new http2 muxer rollout (canary). I think rollout started 02:10 UTC.

mike_engineer: Ok, likely culprit. Our http2 muxer does a small rebuffer window to reduce small-packet overhead; it can introduce a flush delay for tiny follow-up chunks. We defaulted a 3s coalesce window in canary for throughput gains. :grimacing:

ingrid_sre: Can we confirm by forcing bypass of muxer? Suggest steps for customer: set header `x-redwood-stream-mode: flush-immediate` or call non-streaming endpoint as workaround. Also verify if `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` vs SSE over h2 path differs.

jordan_support: Customer tried disabling streaming on their side and saw end-to-end latency drop for their use case (they got full payload faster). They asked for a hotfix rather than switching client logic.

mike_engineer: Short-term mitigation: add per-customer override to disable the coalesce window (config key `stream.coalesce_ms`). I'll push a canary rollback for us-west-2 to 02:05 config for customers on the enterprise override list. Longer-term: lower coalesce to 100ms and add heuristics to not apply to first N chunks.

ingrid_sre: I'll open a rollback runbook and coordinate with deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: roll-out job queued: rollback http2-muxer-coalesce -> us-west-2. ETA 10m. CI checks passed.

sarah_support: Thanks team. I'll reply to Acme with repro steps to confirm header workaround and estimate 15-30m for hotfix rollback. Also adding note to ticket to collect any curl traces and client TCP stack if still repros after rollback.

mike_engineer: Follow-ups: add metric `stream.first_chunk_gap_ms` and alert on p99 > 1s for streaming routes; add small test in smoke suite to detect regressions when changing coalescing. Will file PR today.

jordan_support: perfect. I'll mark ticket "wip - eng rollback in progress" and post update once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
